items.title: Lou Marini interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 15, 2023

ctx.x: Only like James takes priority, and we know that usually we’re going to be playing in the beginning of the summer. And so I just sort of make sure that I have open space you know. But also, the business has changed so much now. You know for instance doing clinics. I did a bunch of them this year but they usually want you to commit so far in advance that it’s difficult to commit to doing a clinic in March when you know that there’s a likelihood that the Blues Brothers Band is liable to go to Japan. And so I try to…

with Miles were my colleagues. I overlapped them in the studios. And they were very welcoming and mentors really with advice. So through the 70s and the first half of the 80s we had a busy studio scene going. Then the computers and drum machines and synthesizers began to eke — cut into our business and things, and you went from having ten big companies that did most of the music to a thousand in-house one-man guys who hired the guy that he knew from the University of Alabama to play on his jingle. You know that’s…
I’m just reading a book — I got to know Joe Wilder.
